problem_type: Main-process event loop parked on a synchronous child-process wait
symptom: 0.23.1: while results land, the app stops responding — clicks do nothing and Settings does not open right away; the user reports other versions do not feel this way.
direct_cause: electron/assets/generatedMediaDecode.ts ran ffmpeg with spawnSync in the main process to verify every generated output before it was written (wait ceiling 12–120 s by size). Every sync IPC from the renderer, every async IPC reply and window event waited behind it. History: a synchronous decode check already existed in v0.22.5 (inside projectAssetStore); v0.23.0 (#938, 8ddb06250) moved it to generatedMediaDecode.ts, switched it to a framehash decode and raised the size-scaled wait ceiling to 120 s, making the wait heavier; v0.23.1 inherits it.
class_root: Nothing structurally stops main-process code from waiting synchronously on an external process: spawnSync / execFileSync / execSync are as easy to write as their async forms, finish in tens of milliseconds on small fixtures, and the only existing registry for child processes (offLedgerEgress) asks whether a process may spend money, not whether it blocks the main loop.
affected_population: Every generated image / video / audio written through writeAsset, writeDeterministicAsset, moveAssetFile or copyAssetFile with meta.kind=generated (provider results, MCP materialization, Codex / Antigravity / Dreamina local results, custom calls, screenshots, frame extraction, trim, depth video, camera-move)
All platforms; worst on large videos, slow disks and machines with real-time antivirus scanning
entry_points: projectAssetStore.validatedGeneratedMeta — the one caller of verifyGeneratedMediaDecodes
writeAsset / writeDeterministicAsset / moveAssetFile / copyAssetFile — the four writers that call validatedGeneratedMeta
LocalTaskJobs.query — the synchronous import commit used by the Antigravity local provider

external_sources.purpose: Electron performance guide: the main process must not block on I/O or long work; use asynchronous child processes.

execFile timeout / maxBuffer / killed semantics used to map the asynchronous run back onto the existing verdict facts (also verified empirically with a real child for timeout, maxBuffer, non-zero exit and ENOENT).

invariants: Main-process production code under electron/ never waits synchronously on an external process (spawnSync / execFileSync / execSync count is zero outside one path-listed E2E fixture).
A generated output is verified before it is published; the verdict kinds, timeout ceiling and fail-closed behavior are unchanged.

After verification, choosing the path, writing bytes, writing the sidecar and broadcasting is one synchronous critical section with no await, so concurrent writes of one deterministic asset cannot interleave.
A local task's import is single-flight: overlapping queries share one import and cancellation waits for it to settle.

The bytes that are verified are the bytes that are published: every writer pins one boundary-owned copy (PinnedAssetBytes, produced only by verifiedAssetBytes.ts) before any await, and sniffing, hashing, decode verification and the disk write all consume that copy; the decoder never reads a caller-owned path.

A write that waited on verification lands in the project it was started for or nowhere: every async writer captures AssetWriteContext before the wait, re-asserts it before publishing and writes under the captured root.

door_reduction.why_not: The doors are the callers of the asset writers (provider results, local providers, screenshots, frame tools, onboarding seed, browser capture). Each is a distinct product entry that legitimately writes assets; the fix does not merge them because they already converge on one verification boundary (validatedGeneratedMeta → verifyGeneratedMediaDecodes), which is the one that became asynchronous. Every door now awaits it; tsc plus the test-type gate reject an un-awaited caller. verifiedAssetBytes.ts is the new home of the one verification door (split out of projectAssetStore for the 800-line limit); pinAssetBytes is a new door by design — the only way bytes enter verification.

generality_proof: The decode verdict has exactly one caller (door-map: verifyGeneratedMediaDecodes → projectAssetStore.validatedGeneratedMeta) and validatedGeneratedMeta is the only gate all four writers pass through; making the verifier asynchronous makes every one of the 16 writeAsset doors, 3 writeDeterministicAsset doors and 2 moveAssetFile doors asynchronous at once. The class (any synchronous child wait in the main process) is closed by the new check-heavy-path rule, which scans every electron/ production file, not only the reported one. The waiting window is closed for both things that can change during it: bytes (PinnedAssetBytes is the only type validatedGeneratedMeta accepts and the only thing the writers publish) and the target project (all four writers consume the existing identity boundary captureAssetWriteContext, owned by the project-binding concept, before the wait and re-assert it before publishing).

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The only way the decode check runs ffmpeg: an asynchronous child with timeout kill and output cap, translated into the same facts the verdict always read.
Awaited by every writer before its synchronous publish section; fails closed before disk.
Single-flight import so the now-asynchronous commit cannot interleave with a second query or a cancellation.
The only producers of PinnedAssetBytes (with readPinnedAssetFile): a copy owned by the write boundary that no caller can mutate during the asynchronous wait (V-1208-1).

same_class_entry_points.evidence: async; awaits validatedGeneratedMeta; projectAssetStore.test.ts 'writeAsset verifies a generated video without parking the main loop' was red before.
async; same main-loop test plus concurrent same-key writes test.
async; source bytes read with fs.promises; main-loop test red before.
Already async; now awaits the asynchronous verifier.

E2E fixture renderer; only constructed when isProductionRunE2eFixtureEnabled (NOMI_E2E and NOMI_E2E_PRODUCTION_FIXTURE, plus NOMI_E2E_PACKAGED_FIXTURE in packaged builds). Listed by exact path in the gate's exemption with that reason.

recurrence.reason: Any future local media step (transcode, probe, extract) can reach for a synchronous child-process call; it passes every test on small fixtures and only freezes on user machines.
same_class_scan: rg -n '\b(spawnSync|execFileSync|execSync)\b' electron --type ts: 2 production files (generatedMediaDecode.ts — fixed; productionRunE2eFixture.ts — gated fixture, exempted by path)
electron/offLedgerEgress.structure.test.ts AST scan of child-process-sync primitives: same two files
node scripts/door-map.mjs verifyGeneratedMediaDecodes / validatedGeneratedMeta / writeAsset / writeDeterministicAsset / moveAssetFile

prevention.invariant: The decode check only exists as an asynchronous child (runDecoder); electron/ production code contains no spawnSync / execFileSync / execSync outside the path-listed E2E fixture (check:heavy-path main-sync-child-process, baseline 0).
prevention.failure_mode: check:heavy-path exits 1 and prints file:line with the asynchronous replacement.
prevention.strategy: Gate by presence, not by count (baseline 0), like unguarded-fsync: deleting one allowed call and adding a new one cannot keep the gate green. The verifier itself only exists in asynchronous form, so no writer can call it synchronously.

legacy_paths.rationale: The spawnSync defaultRun is deleted in the same change; there is no synchronous fallback. The offLedgerEgress registry entry for the synchronous decode is removed with it.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Node's built-in child_process.execFile replaces spawnSync; no third-party runtime is involved and the bundled ffmpeg and its invocation are unchanged.

migration: No stored data changes. Writers became async; every production caller was updated to await (tsc and the test-type gate reject a synchronous fake or an un-awaited Promise used as a record).
residual_risks: Other synchronous fs work on large files in the main process (readFileSync of a whole video in writeDeterministicAsset's existing-file hash, sha256 of large buffers) still runs on the main loop; it is CPU / disk work, not a child wait, and needs measurement before a fix (C-perfguide M02).

An asynchronous decode spawned inside a paid dispatch is now visible to the dispatch ledger's child_process channel, which can only make a failed dispatch read as 'unknown' rather than 'never sent' — the conservative direction.
If the app quits while a decode child is running, the child is bounded by its timeout but is not killed on quit; the scratch file it reads is left for the OS temp cleaner.

Pinning copies the caller buffer once (a large video costs one extra transient copy in main-process memory); path-based writers that verify content now read the file into memory instead of renaming it.
